name: Two Pendant Three-Edge Arms Determine a Small Tree Core Uniquely
statement: Let a tree be obtained from a path core of order one, two, or three by attaching two internally vertex-disjoint pendant paths of length three, each meeting the core only at its initial vertex. The core and the unordered pair of attached paths are uniquely determined by the resulting tree among decompositions with the same core order.
proof: For core orders one and two, the center or central edge identifies the core unless both arms meet one endpoint, in which case the unique degree-three vertex and branch lengths $1,3,3$ do. For a three-vertex core, the four attachment patterns are distinguished respectively by the central three-vertex path, branch lengths $2,3,3$, degree four with branch lengths $1,1,3,3$, or branch lengths $1,3,4$. In each case these intrinsic degrees and branch lengths recover the core and both arms.
